I found one bug in the uncommitted changes. It's in `billing/invoice.py:19`, in `billable_hours`.

`session.start` and `session.end` are both timezone-aware values in the same zone object. Python then subtracts them as plain wall-clock times and ignores the UTC offset change at a daylight-saving switch.

I confirmed this with a quick check: a real one-hour session on 2026-03-08 (06:30 to 07:30 UTC, New York) shows as 01:30 EST to 03:30 EDT. The subtraction gives 2 hours, so the customer is billed 2 hours instead of 1, an overcharge of 180 cents. Sessions that cross the fall-back switch are undercounted in the same way.

The fix is to convert both times to UTC before subtracting, for example `(end.astimezone(timezone.utc) - start.astimezone(timezone.utc)).total_seconds()`.

The new tests don't catch this because none of their sessions cross a daylight-saving switch. Adding a test with one that does would cover it. I didn't run the test suite.

findings.summary: billable_hours subtracts session.end - session.start, but both are aware datetimes sharing the same ZoneInfo tzinfo, so Python subtracts naive wall-clock time and ignores the UTC offset change at DST transitions.
findings.failure_scenario: An a-100 session from 06:30 UTC to 07:30 UTC on 2026-03-08 (a real 1 hour) becomes 01:30 EST to 03:30 EDT. The subtraction yields 2:00:00, so billable_hours returns 2 and the customer is overcharged one hour (180 cents). In the fall-back case the session is undercounted. Fix: convert both to UTC first, e.g. (session.end.astimezone(timezone.utc) - session.start.astimezone(timezone.utc)).total_seconds().
